content: 1. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dexlanoprazole by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dexlanoprazole by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine transdermal by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Initiate with lower doses and monitor for serotonin syndrome, especially during dextroamphetamine initiation or dose escalation. Discontinue dextroamphetamine transdermal and CYP2D6 inhibitors if serotonin syndrome occurs. 4. DHEA (herbal supplement) increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. A reduced dose of diazepam may be necessary. 6. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of diazepam buccal by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of diazepam buccal by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 8. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the elimination rate of diazepam, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 9. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of diazepam intranasal by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of diazepam intranasal by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 11. Darunavir increases the effects of diazoxide by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors exist. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating concomitant drugs. Adjust the digoxin dose by approximately 30-50% or modify dosing frequency and continue monitoring. 13. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of didanosine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Administer didanosine 1 hour before or 2 hours after darunavir/ritonavir. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Significant changes in plasma levels of estrogen and progestin have been observed with HIV protease inhibitors. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 15. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 17. Diltiazem increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Consider avoiding the concomitant use of protease inhibitors and nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (CCBs). Monitor for CCB toxicities if a protease inhibitor is initiated or its dose is increased. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 19. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider reducing docetaxel dosing by 50% if concomitant administration cannot be avoided. 21. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of doravirine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of doravirine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of doxepin by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. 24. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. 26. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. 27. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of drospirenone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 28. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor increases duvelisib AUC, which may increase the risk of duvelisib toxicities. 29. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both darunavir and efavirenz increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 30. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Coadministration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 31. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely.
